newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks track Wall Street, bonds to close up.
newsitem.headline: French stocks track Wall Street, bonds to close up.

text.p: French stocks staged a partial rebound on Friday after investors were encouraged by higher bond prices and a rise on Wall Street, brokers said.
The bourse also took heart from the appointments to the Bank of France's monetary policy council of two candidates viewed as more likely to favour lower interest rates, they said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index, which fell 2.54 percent on Thursday, recovered 25.79 points, or 1.14 percent, to close at 2,282.76. For the week, it was down 1.05 percent.
The CAC January futures contract rose 32 points to 2,288.
Volume was a relatively light 3.33 billion francs.

Brokers expect more normal levels of activity next week when players return from holiday. "The New Year will really begin on Monday," a portfolio manager said, adding that the bourse generally performs well at the start of the year.

The market welcomed the appointments of monetary "doves" Pierre Guillen, former head of the employers' federation CNPF, and Jean-Rene Bernard, former deputy governor at property lender Credit Foncier, to the nine-member monetary policy council.
But the bourse's primary focus is on U.S. interest rates, with investors fearing that increases to quell inflationary pressures could end Wall Street's bull run.
The market will be watching closely next week for key U.S. indicators such as durable goods orders on Tuesday, jobless claims and wholesale prices on Thursday.

* The biggest gainers on the bourse on Friday were often the previous day's top losers. Compagnie Bancaire, among them, finished up 5.80 percent at 620 francs. Rhone-Poulenc rose 2.48 percent to 173.50.

* The car sector showed less resilience. PSA Peugeot Citroen shares recouped 1.26 percent, or less than a third of Thursday's loss on 1996 car sales data showing the French industry lost market share. They closed at 562 francs.
Renault closed up 0.47 percent at 108 francs.
* Freezing weather in Europe boosted shares in energy groups Total, up 2.21 percent at 416 francs, and Elf-Aquitaine, up 1.95 percent at 471.50.
* Axa closed up 1.23 percent at 330 francs. It said its National Mutual unit would contribute 291 million francs to 1996 profit, more than double its 1995 contribution.

* Cie des Salins du Midi, which resumed trading on Friday for the first time since December 23, was the top gainer with a 38 percent rise to 607 francs, close to the 614 franc per share offer proposed on Tuesday by Morton International.

Morton said it would buy the 50.8 percent controlling stake in Cie des Salins from a Compagnie de Suez subsidiary and offer the same price to minority shareholders. The bid values Cie des Salins at 1.5 billion francs.

* Insurer Assurances Generales de France (AGF) finished up 2.63 percent at 168.10. News magazine La Vie Francaise ran an article saying AGF may lack the critical mass to go up against newly merged Axa-UAP entity and may become a takeover target.
